ops.body:
Why the File Provider data socket (pool.FPBridgeSocketPath) and the daemon's FP bridge serve loop are shaped the way they are.

## Socket location
- The daemon binds the socket; the sandboxed FP extension dials it for computed content. It MUST live in the App Group container (~/Library/Group Containers/<AppGroupID>/) — the one location BOTH sides may touch: the sandboxed appex gets blanket container access, and the daemon is an entitled group member.
- The daemon resolves that container at runtime via NSFileManager containerURLForSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier: (fusekit's appgroup package, objc over purego, still CGO_ENABLED=0) — NEVER a raw filepath.Join of ~/Library/Group Containers. Resolving via containerURL is one of Apple's three preconditions for a prompt-free grant; a hand-built path still prompts. pool.FPBridgeSocketPath is display/diagnostic only now.
- Sandbox file temp-exceptions do NOT cover AF_UNIX connect — connect(2) is a network-outbound operation, so a socket parked anywhere else is unreachable from the appex no matter what file exceptions it holds.
- The leaf is deliberately short ("b.sock") to keep the full path under the 104-byte sun_path limit.

## TCC consent gating (startFPBridge / serveFPBridge) — bundle+profile model, cc-pool v0.59.0+
- macOS gates the group container behind a TCC consent (kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData). tccd keys a BARE executable's grant row by its RESOLVED PATH (client_type=1), so every keg upgrade minted a fresh path client and re-prompted — and worse, macOS fallback consent for an unauthorized group claim is INSTANCE-scoped, so no TCC-row keying trick could ever make it durable. The v0.45.0 dotted identifier (csreq-only) and the v0.49.1 stable-path re-exec (~/.cc-pool/bin/cc-pool) were both this dead end; BOTH are deleted.
- THE FIX (v0.59.0, tag bd55a87b): the daemon ships as CCPoolDaemon.app in the formula's libexec — a real bundle (CFBundleIdentifier com.yasyf.cc-pool.daemon) with an embedded Developer ID provisioning profile that authorizes the app group (the portal mints the team wildcard SXKCTF23Q2.*, which authorizes SXKCTF23Q2.ccp). A bundled main executable + containerURL + a profile-authorized group claim is Apple's no-prompt contract; tccd then keys the grant to the bundle IDENTIFIER (client_type=0), durable across upgrades. The LaunchAgent launches opt_libexec/CCPoolDaemon.app/Contents/MacOS/cc-pool (pool.DaemonBinaryPath, which EvalSymlinks the Homebrew bin symlink to reach the keg libexec). CCPoolStatus.app + the FP appex carry their own DevID profiles (cc-pool Status Host / FileProvider DevID) the same way.
- Adhoc/unsigned/source builds and any bundle WITHOUT the embedded profile fall back to the instance-scoped prompt (an "unprofiled build") — that is the only remaining case fpConsentPending should trip. The daemon log token to watch is "app-group-container consent" (load-bearing: the VM scenario greps it).
- The container MkdirAll runs INSIDE the retried serve loop (serveFPBridge), never on startFPBridge's caller path: it can hang on a pending prompt (unprofiled build) or fail while consent is denied, and retrying picks up a late approval.
- serveFPBridge retries abnormal exits with a capped backoff: every FP domain's computed content depends on this one bridge, so transient failures must self-heal rather than wait out a daemon restart. ctx cancellation cuts the backoff sleep short so wg.Wait never blocks on a sleeping retry.
- startFPBridge waits only a bounded fpBridgeWait for the socket to accept. If it doesn't come up while the daemon is alive AND no hard bind error was recorded, that is the consent-pending signature (unprofiled build): flagged on fpConsentPending for status/doctor, cleared by a watchdog the moment the socket lands. `ccp fp consent` is now a pure DIAGNOSTIC (probes the daemon; no more stable-binary exec). A leftover ~/.cc-pool/bin is reported + --fix-removed by a doctor rung (pool.LegacyStableBinDir).
- os.ErrPermission from the bind path is the TCC denied/parked signature (stays eligible for consent-pending); any other error is a genuine bind failure reported as fpBridgeHardErr, never as a consent prompt.

## Shared source
startFPBridge is the sibling of startContentBridge, sharing the SAME PoolContentSource instance: the Source contract requires concurrency safety, and the write-through mutex is package-level, so write-throughs serialize across both bridge servers in the one daemon process.

## Live proof
The two-upgrade no-prompt proof runs via runbook b03f9f95 on both Macs (VM rehearsal was skipped — host Local Network TCC blocked it; see note ed5a74dc). Portal artifacts + profile UUIDs/names in note eac747e9.

ops.when: working on the daemon's File Provider bridge (startFPBridge/serveFPBridge), FPBridgeSocketPath, the daemon .app bundle / provisioning profile, app-group-container consent, or 'bridge socket not accepting' diagnoses
